source_judgment_basis: No remaining material source error, omission or unsupported consequential decision was found after full declared-scope semantic assessment and independent primary checks. Minor source precision/fidelity/navigation and evidence-access limitations are explicit. Corrected lineage defects are retained as history, not scored as remaining final defects.

axes.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axes.assessment: The final is a five-collection planning proposal, not a build or legal determination. All eight clauses are explicitly reconciled. It preserves registrar/metadata-lead authority, exact supplied statement plus origin/history, both authorized optional features, and all four negative constraints. No license, thumbnail permission, restricted scrape, unknown-to-public-domain conversion or nonexistent deployment is prescribed. Source-specific permissions and collection endpoints are honestly unresolved owner inputs, after investigation of the relevant public mechanisms.

axes.name: Consequential source claims: subject, operation, version, defaults, type, domain and exceptions
axes.assessment: Independently checked entity/rights subjects, vocabulary-family applicability, licenses/CC0/PDM, OAI deletion/date/format/token conditions, DPLA MAP/API/partner terms, EDM 5.2.7, IIIF 3.0 typed URI/text and viewer scope, SKOS mapping semantics, PROV responsibility, Omeka import/export roles and compatibility, and pinned NARA source history. The final uses documentation as conditional planning evidence. No source supports actual feeds/export permissions for the unspecified collections, and the final does not claim them. Historical gate summary is slightly overcompressed. Current RightsStatements FAQ uses HTTPS examples while IIIF 3.0 describes HTTP; preserving original source identifiers prevents a wrong normalization rule.

axes.name: Useful unfamiliar discovery, competing/analogous approaches, implementation/history and opportunity breadth
axes.assessment: Discovery independently found DPLA/Europeana hub patterns, conditional OAI-PMH harvesting, IIIF presentation, RightsStatements/CC distinctions, SKOS/PROV analogues, enrichment and export opportunities. After reveal, Omeka S was researched as an editorial publisher rather than assumed to be an aggregator. The final meaningfully compares network-controlled history versus hub reach/intermediary conditions and carries a pinned deletion fix plus ESE mapping migration into per-collection controls. This is useful investigation, not vacuous caution. One supplementary live-federation fallback is lost, without material loss of required workflow/option coverage.

axes.name: Wrong criticism/corrections/rejections and exact plan dispositions
axes.assessment: The plan’s binary mapping, universal badge, discarded URI and link-only provenance assumptions are correctly rejected. Unattached history and the two-record all-collection validation idea are replaced by documented mechanisms and source-specific prospective checks. Optional capabilities remain optional and owner constraints remain binding. C1 is independently supported and corrected; C2 is accepted as an operational terms gate using relationship-specific evidence, not a blanket legal rule; C3 accurately records conflicting source-version signals; C4 appropriately remains a nonempirical method contrast. No material wrong criticism, false correction or unsupported scope rejection remains.

axes.name: Supported meaning preserved through discovery, draft, critique and final
axes.assessment: The draft/final carry the core discovery recommendation, sources and historical mechanisms, raw URI/attribution provenance, explicit owner routing, useful tool/analogue roles, both optional features, uncertainties and validation boundaries. Final corrections add term-specific scope and source-operation authorization without replacing the proposal with a patch list. Investigator and critic source maps are embedded unchanged under distinct namespaces, corroborating identity only; semantic comparison, not those hashes, establishes preservation. Minor loss of a live-federation alternative and imperfect relative locators remain.

axes.name: Meaningful proposed versus executed validation and oracle applicability
axes.assessment: Executed items are source reading, read-only pinned history inspection and input/reveal/file operations; none is presented as successful catalog operation. Five-source compatibility, UI/export operation and legal/owner decisions remain NOT RUN. Proposed checks discriminate source scope/missing/conflict states, exact URI preservation, mapping ambiguity, updates/deletion policies/recovery and export exclusions. Their oracle is the original assertion plus selected feed/profile/owner rules, not a thumbnail or a synthesized permission boolean. No local executable witness is claimed. Public code inspection proves a source-level mechanism, not deployment success; upstream executed-read claims lack preserved transcripts. Validation priorities are expressed mainly by prerequisites and order, not an explicit ranked column.
